Lily was a little girl who liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Anna, who had a pink dress and a charming smile. Lily always took Anna with her when she went out.

One day, Lily and her mom went to visit her grandma, who lived in a big house. Lily was happy to see her grandma, who gave her a hug and a cookie. But she was also curious about the other rooms in the house. She asked her mom if she could explore.

Lily nodded and ran off with Anna. She saw many doors, some open and some closed. She peeked into some of the open ones and saw a bedroom, a bathroom, a kitchen, and a library. She wondered what was behind the closed ones.

Sara looks around the room. She sees many cars, but not Ben. She thinks he is very good at hiding. She walks to the other side of the room and sees a helpful lady. The lady wears a badge that says "Museum Guide". Sara asks the lady, "Have you seen my brother? He is hiding from me."

The lady smiles and says, "I think I have. He is under the car with the shiny hood. Do you want me to show you?"

Sara nods and says, "Yes, please. Thank you for being helpful."

The lady takes Sara to the car and points under the hood. Sara sees Ben's feet sticking out. She says, "I found you, Ben! You are a good hider, but the lady helped me."

Ben crawls out from under the car and says, "You are a good finder, Sara. And the lady is very nice. Can we say thank you to her?"

Sara and Ben smile and say, "We do. We love the museum. And we love playing hide and seek."

Tom saw the grill nearby and had an idea. He thought he could make his car go even faster if he put it on the grill. He did not think about how hot the grill was or how it could hurt his car. He ran to the grill and threw his car on it. He shouted, "Look, Jen, my car is on fire! I win!"

Jen saw what Tom did and felt scared and sad. She knew the grill was dangerous and she loved her brother. She did not want him to get burned or lose his car. She ran to the grill and tried to grab Tom's car. But the car was too hot and it burned her hand. She screamed and dropped the car. She started to cry.

Tom heard Jen's scream and saw her hand. He realized he had done a bad thing. He felt sorry and ashamed. He ran to Jen and hugged her. He said, "I'm sorry, Jen, I'm sorry. I was silly and mean. Are you okay?"

Lily was excited to try it out. She went over to the flowers and held the rod up to them. "Wow!" she exclaimed. "These flowers are taller than I thought!"

Lily was curious. She held the rod up to herself and saw that she had grown a little bit since the last time she measured. She was so happy and proud of herself. From that day on, Lily used her new rod to measure everything she could find.

Once upon a time, there was a big whale. He was very happy swimming in the ocean. One day, he met a little fish. The fish asked, "Do you have any food to supply me?" The whale replied, "I don't have any food, but I can take you to a place where you can find some."

The whale took the little fish to a beautiful orange reef. The fish was so happy to see all the food he could eat. The whale said goodbye and swam away. But as the little fish was eating, a big shark came and ate him up. The whale never saw the little fish again.

The end.

Lily thought about this for a moment and then asked, "Does it weigh a lot?"

"Yes, it's pretty heavy," said Grandma.

That night, Lily was sleeping in the guest room when she heard a strange noise. She looked up and saw a ghost floating in the air! The ghost was persistent and wouldn't go away. 

Lily was scared and ran to her grandma's room. "Grandma, there's a ghost in my room!" she cried.

Grandma went to investigate and found that the old clock had stopped working. She knew just what to do. She fixed the clock and the ghost disappeared. From then on, Lily loved the clock even more and would always ask, "Grandma, can we weigh the clock again?"

Once upon a time there was an orange frog called Sam. Sam lived in a small pond near a wood. Everyday Sam would sun himself on a rock in the middle of the pond.

One day, Sam heard a noise. He hopped out of the pond to see what was happening. He saw two animals, a rabbit and a squirrel, squabbling by a tree. The rabbit and the squirrel were shouting at each other and their fur was all ruffled. 

Sam hopped over to them and he said, "What is wrong here? Why are you both so angry?" 

The rabbit said, "That squirrel won't share his nuts with me." 

The squirrel said, "But you didn't ask nicely!"

Sam thought for a moment and said, "Maybe you could both take turns? That would be fairer." 

The rabbit and the squirrel thought that was a good idea. So the squirrel gave some of his nuts to the rabbit and the rabbit shared some apples with the squirrel. After that they both said their goodbyes and went their separate ways. 

Sam watched them go and was very pleased that he had been able to help out. Then he hopped back into the pond and sunned himself, feeling very content.

Henry leaned into his mommy's side. He was still a bit frightened. They entered the store and Mommy went to get the powder. He waited for her next to the cash register and leaned against the wall. The cashier was nice and smiled at him.

Mommy came back carrying a big bag of powder. Henry felt his fears melting away. Mommy put her arm around him and hugged him tight. She said it was time to go home. 

Henry leaned against his mommy's side as they walked out of the store. He was still a bit scared but he was also feeling brave and safe. He couldn't wait to get back to his cozy bed.

Bob thanked the kind bird and hopped away. He kept his eyes on the path until he reached the other side of the forest. Finally, he made it back home in time for dinner.

The frog cheered excitedly. He wanted to gain strength, so he hopped around the meadow even faster than before. He practiced and practiced, and soon he felt stronger. 

The green frog was so proud of himself. He hopped up high into the sky and proudly saw the green symbol still shining brilliantly. He knew he had gained strength!

Mama played a song on the record player. It was a happy, bouncy tune.
Joey was excited. He started to dance. He did a silly jig and spun around in circles.
Mama said, "Wow, Joey! You are such a great dancer!"
Joey smiled and said, "Yes, I am!"

Mama and Joey danced for a while. They danced to the music and laughed a lot. Joey was having a great time. 
But then the music stopped. Mama said it was time to go inside. 
Joey said, "But Mama, the music was so fun! Can't we stay outside a little bit longer?"
Mama smiled and said, "No, Joey. It's dull outside now. Let's go in and we can record another song tomorrow." 
Joey smiled and said, "Okay, Mama!" He gave her a hug and they went inside.

Once upon a time there was a mommy and her baby. Mommy wanted to keep the baby safe, so she taught the baby to not touch anything yellow. 

Mommy said, "Baby, please don't touch the yellow because it might be dangerous. It's better to be safe and prevent any harm."

But one day, the baby saw a yellow butterfly fluttering around. The butterfly was so pretty, and it looked harmless.

The baby asked, "Mommy, can I touch the butterfly?"

Mommy said, "Yes, you can, baby. That butterfly is harmless and won't hurt you. But remember, don't touch the yellow things that don't look harmless."

The baby nodded and smiled. From then on, the baby knew to be careful when it came to yellow.

Micky was a funny little mouse. He liked to do things differently. One day, he had an idea for a new game.

Micky went over to his friend Daisy's house. "Let's play a game!", he said. Daisy smiled.

Micky asked Daisy to stand on one foot and balance a juice bottle on her neck. They both had a lot of fun. Micky was very creative with his ideas.

Daisy said, "Wow, this is fun!" Micky grinned and said, "I like to do things differently."

They played the game for hours. Daisy got better and better at balancing the juice bottle.

At the end of the day, they hugged and said goodbye. Both of them had had a fun and creative day playing the balancing game.

Once upon a time there was a wealthy cup who lived in an enormous castle. Every day the cup would march through the castle's grand hallways, admiring its beauty.

One day, the cup was strolling through the corridors when it ran into a tiny mouse. The cup stopped and asked the mouse, "What are you doing here?" The mouse replied, "I am looking for food. I haven't eaten anything in days!"

The cup felt sorry for the mouse and decided to help. It marched to the castle kitchen and brought back a cup filled with cheese. The mouse was thrilled and thanked the cup for its help.

The cup smiled and said, "You're welcome! It's so important to help those who are less fortunate than us." The mouse nodded in agreement and happily scurried off to enjoy its meal. 

From then on, the wealthy cup was known as the most generous in the castle.

"Hello," said Lucy.

The dog looked up and smiled. "Hello," said the dog. "My name is Max. What's your name?"

"My name is Lucy," said Lucy. "I'm wandering through this country."

Max barked happily. "I'd be glad to show you around!"

So Lucy and Max went on a journey together and saw many wonderful things. Everywhere they went, people and animals said hello to them. Lucy had a great time and felt very cheerful. 

At the end of their journey, Max said goodbye and went back to the castle. Lucy waved to him and went on her way. She was happy she had such a fun adventure.

"Hi, Faucet," she said. "You're so purple! I love skipping around you."

The faucet wasn't very loud, but it answered in a small voice.

"Thank you, Sarah," it said. "I like it when you skip. Please keep skipping around me."

So Sarah kept skipping around the faucet. Faster and faster she skipped until the faucet was a blur of purple spinning around her. She giggled and skipped and twirled until she was too tired to keep going.

"That was so much fun," Sarah said and gave the faucet a big smile. "Let's skip again soon!"

Tommy wanted to fly too. He waved his hands and leaped into the air, trying to fly after the aeroplane. His mom heard him and came over, putting her hands on his shoulders.

"You can't fly, Tommy. But don't worry. I have a surprise for you," said his mom, and she snapped her fingers.

Suddenly, the garden filled with floating bubbles! Tommy giggled with joy and jumped up and down, trying to catch them. Each time he popped one, Tommy laughed and clapped his hands. He even managed to catch a few in his hands and blow them away. It was so much fun!

When all the bubbles had snapped away, Tommy flopped on the grass and looked up at the sky. He thought about the aeroplane he had seen earlier, wishing he could take a journey and explore the world. But for now, he was just happy to watch the clouds drift by, peaceful and free.

Sophie struck her stick against it and the sparkles stopped. She looked closer and saw something was shining in the darkness. It was a diamond! 

Surprised, Sophie said out loud, "I found a diamond!"

Suddenly, she heard a voice. It came from a man who was hiding in the corner of the mine. He said, "Well, this diamond is mine." 

Sophie was not scared. She was thoughtful. She asked the man, "If I give the diamond to you, can I explore the mine?" 

The man thought for a moment and said, "Yes, but be careful."

Sophie thanked him and gave the diamond to the man. She explored the mine and had a great adventure. She went home with many stories to tell.

John asked his mom, "Mom, what is that sound?"

His mom smiled and said, "It's the call of a bird."

John was so excited! He wanted to find it, so he asked his mom, "Can we go find it?"

His mom said, "Yes, we can go look for it. You can take the way to the park."

So, John and his mom went for a walk. Soon, John spotted a bright yellow bird, sitting on a tree branch. John smiled and pointed to the bird.

"Mom, look at that bird!" he said.

His mom smiled. "That's the bird that was calling!" she said.

John laughed and waved. The bird waved back and then flew away.

John and his mom watched it fly away until it was out of sight. They had a lot of fun that day, and John would never forget the call of the bright yellow bird.

Once upon a time there was a bear named Bob who lived in the woods. One day, Bob felt very sleepy and he didn't feel like doing anything. Unfortunately, he had to find some food, so he started to walk around to look for something to eat.

Suddenly, Bob heard a loud noise. He was a bit scared so he slowly peeked around the corner. What he saw made him very surprised! It was two foxes, arguing and fighting over something. Bob felt bad for them, so he decided to try and help.

He stepped into the clearing and said, "Hey! Why are you fighting?"

The foxes looked at Bob and stopped. The bigger fox said, "This is my food, but the other fox said that it was his too."

Bob thought for a minute, then he said, "I have an idea. Why don't you both step back and I'll increase the amount of food so that there's enough for both of you?"

The foxes looked at each other and then agreed with Bob's plan. As Bob had promised, he added more food so that both of the foxes could have equal amounts. The foxes thanked him and promised him to not fight again.

Bob was glad that he could help. He felt really happy as he continued his journey to find food.

After they were done, Tom thanked Sam and said, "Thank you, Sam. You are a good friend." Sam smiled and said, "You're welcome, Tom. I am always here to help you." And from that day on, they became the best of friends and always helped each other when they needed it.

Once upon a time, there was a small cat named Kitty. Kitty liked to play with her friends, but sometimes she was not nice. One day, Kitty took her friend's toy without asking.

Kitty's friend, Doggy, said, "Kitty, that's my toy! Please give it back!" But Kitty didn't want to give it back. She ran away with the toy and hid it under a tree.

Soon, the other animals found out what Kitty did. They were very angry. They said, "Kitty, you must become good, or you will go to jail." But Kitty didn't listen to them.

One day, the animals caught Kitty taking another toy. They said, "Now you must go to jail." They put Kitty in a small jail made of sticks.

Kitty was sad, and she did not like the bad ending. She wished she had been good and listened to her friends.

Once upon a time, a little boy named Tim went to school. His teacher, Miss Kate, was very nice. Tim had many friends who were pupils too. They played and learned together. One day, Tim saw a big, shiny toy car in a shop. It was very expensive, but he wanted it so much.

Tim asked his mom, "Can I have the expensive toy car, please?" His mom said, "No, it is too much money. We cannot buy it." Tim was sad, but he had an idea. He thought he could take the toy car without his mom knowing.

The next day, Tim went to the shop and took the toy car. He hid it in his bag and went to school. When he got to school, he showed his friends the toy car. They all wanted to play with it. Tim let them play with the car, but he didn't tell them he took it from the shop.

Miss Kate saw the pupils playing with the expensive toy car. She knew it was not Tim's car. She asked Tim, "Where did you get this car?" Tim didn't want to tell the truth. He lied and said, "My mom bought it for me." Miss Kate knew Tim was not telling the truth. She called his mom and found out he took the car from the shop.

Tim got in big trouble. His mom was very sad and angry. She made Tim return the toy car to the shop and say sorry. Tim learned that taking things without asking is wrong. He felt bad and promised never to do it again. But because he lied, his friends and Miss Kate did not trust him anymore. Tim was very sad and lonely.

One day, a cute little girl named Lily went to her garden. She had a small bag of beans. She wanted to grow big bean plants. Lily dug a hole in the ground and put a bean in it. She covered the bean with dirt and gave it some water. "Grow big and strong, little bean," she said.

The next day, Lily saw a small bird in her garden. The bird looked at the place where Lily put the bean. "Are you looking for my bean?" Lily asked the bird. The bird nodded its head. Lily thought the bird was hungry, so she gave it some seeds to eat. "You can visit my bean, but don't eat it, okay?" The bird nodded again and flew away.

Days went by, and Lily took care of her bean every day. The bird came back to visit, too. One day, the bean started to grow into a big, strong plant. Lily was so happy! The bird came back and saw the big bean plant. It nodded its head and flew away. Lily knew that the bird was happy for her and her big bean plant.

"Why are you sad?" Tim asked the bird.

"My nest is wet, and I can't keep my eggs warm," the bird said.

Tim wanted to help the bird. He found a dry spot under a big tree. He helped the bird move her nest there. The bird was happy.

"Thank you, Tim," said the bird. "Now I can keep my eggs warm."

From that day on, Tim and the bird were good friends. They played together every day, even when the ground was wet.

Lily poured some lemon juice into a small bowl for Max. He lapped it up and made a funny face. "It's sour, isn't it, Max?" Lily giggled. Max barked softly, "Woof!" They both laughed and enjoyed the lemon juice together.
